parsed.explanation: The visitor meets a hostile national overlay atop a comparatively protective state. At the border, national rules redefining sex, refusal instructions for discrepant documents or reasonable doubt as to sex, and a possible material-misrepresentation finding carrying lifetime ineligibility are a real traveller-facing exposure, corroborated by foreign advisories and detentions of foreign nationals; national custody conditions are documented as abusive. Inside the state, gender-identity anti-discrimination law covers housing, employment, accommodations, health care and schools, hate-crime enhancements operate, and enforcement is documented in a 2026 civil-rights judgment. But federal single-sex facility rules reach every trans visitor in national buildings, and the state's own record has degraded (minor care bans, surgery-gated birth-certificate changes). Worse than the trained-border tribunal tier, better than entry-denial-with-no-remedy tier.

entry_documents.exposure: National sex redefinition; officers instructed to refuse cases with discrepant documents or reasonable doubt as to sex, and to weigh material misrepresentation supporting lifetime ineligibility; X markers no longer processed; foreign governments issued advisories after detentions of foreign nationals.
entry_documents.protection: Litigation ongoing against the passport policy; several orders enjoined; legal-aid FAQ on document rules; state licences offer X markers.
entry_documents.interaction: Home passport meets national screening; a marker/appearance mismatch can escalate from secondary inspection to fraud-ground refusal or removal.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody documented as forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse for transgender detainees; national corrections model imposes haircuts, hormone removal and psychiatric substitution; prisoner counts no longer reported.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Court challenges to several national orders; no documented consular-access guarantee specific to trans detainees.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A border document dispute can move the traveller into immigration custody, where the documented abuse regime applies regardless of state protections.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National executive order bars transgender people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity, reaching federal buildings nationwide; four states criminalise bathroom use (this state is not among those documented).
federal_state_facilities.protection: State anti-discrimination law covers public accommodations since 2018/2020; no state facility ban documented here.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State accommodations protection does not displace federal facility rules in national buildings; the harshest operative rule governs at each site.

care_services.exposure: State bans gender-affirming medicine and surgery for minors (2024) and puberty blockers, hormones and chest surgery from 2026, with provider discipline and a right to sue; national pressure on youth care and records subpoenas.
care_services.protection: State anti-discrimination extends to health care; conversion therapy for minors banned since 2019; public insurance surgery ban lifted 2017; adult care not restricted by state law.
care_services.interaction: Adult visitors retain state-law service protections; a travelling family with a trans minor faces a documented state care ban and hostile national framing.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups; justice-department reward memo invokes 'radical gender ideology'; health agencies circulated forbidden-terms lists.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State civil-rights enforcement documented; hate-crime enhancements for gender identity since 2019; gay/trans panic defence abolished 2024; 88% local support for protections.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: National rhetorical threat-framing does not automatically bind state police, but it colours federal encounters and border officials' discretion.

minors_guardians.exposure: State bans youth gender-affirming care with a right to sue and provider discipline; national order directs investigation and prosecution of school staff using a minor's preferred name; schools may opt children out of related instruction.
minors_guardians.protection: State anti-bullying law covers gender identity and expression; the state's highest court protected transgender students on privacy/autonomy grounds in 2024.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian travelling with a trans minor meets a state care ban plus national school-prosecution directives; visiting families are not documented as directly prosecuted, but exposure is real.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 72 anti-LGBTQ incidents recorded in the state in 2025 (raw count, no per-capita denominator); local commentary calls the state the region's least safe for transgender residents, an attributed characterisation.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Civil-rights statute enforced — a 2026 court judgment held a man liable for striking a transgender woman; hate-crime enhancements, panic-defence abolition, and high public support for protections.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Reported incidents plus a documented, functioning civil remedy; police and courts have acted for a trans victim rather than against her.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: State birth-certificate change still requires surgery plus a court order; status of national measures and the state's youth-care bans in litigation is unresolved; unclear whether foreign X-marker passports are recognised at entry.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Working state civil-rights enforcement and courts that have blocked several national orders; legal-aid guidance available.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies operate at the state layer but cannot reach border screening or federal custody decisions, where the exposure sits.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra's register denies entry with no effective remedy; here refusal is also possible at the border but is discretionary and evidence-triggered rather than a universal screening register, and in-state the traveller has documented anti-discrimination recourse and functioning courts. Materially safer than this anchor.

Kestrel Isles' extended secondary screening with administrative refusal is the closest match to the national border layer here, but this dossier adds documented abusive immigration custody and a potential lifetime-ineligibility finding, while the state layer is far more protective than that anchor's uneven remedy. Slightly below it.

Meridia's trained border officers and civil-liberties tribunal are absent here: national screening is hostile rather than trained, and federal facility rules exclude rather than accommodate. In-state protections and working civil-rights enforcement keep this dossier from falling further.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is split. Every traveller crosses a national border where sex is redefined, discrepancy or perceived misrepresentation can produce refusal or a lifetime fraud finding, and custody conditions are documented as abusive; federal single-sex facility rules follow the visitor into national buildings. Inside the state, gender-identity anti-discrimination, hate-crime enhancements, an abolished panic defence and a 2026 civil-rights judgment show remedies actually working, with strong public support. State protections cannot pre-empt border or federal custody, so the harshest operative rule governs the journey, holding the rating in the elevated band above trained-border jurisdictions but well below protective-tier ones.
